The explicit public uniformization implication asks for an upgrade from pointwise convergence plus `Monotone F ∧ Continuous F`; this is not enough for the textbook finite-grid proof. The missing formal inputs are: cdf tail limits/tightness (`F -> 0` at -infinity and `F -> 1` at +infinity, or equivalent compact truncation), pathwise monotonicity of each empirical cdf in x, finite-grid/countable-intersection assembly of the a.s. pointwise events, measurability/boundedness of the sup-deviation random variables, and a theorem-level sandwich from grid errors to the global `sSup` deviation. In fact the support premise as stated is too weak: pointwise convergence of empirical cdfs to the continuous monotone zero function can occur when samples drift to +infinity, while the sup deviation stays 1. This rules out proving the old public implication without strengthening it to the actual textbook cdf/iid/tail setting.
